description:
Hey Reachy is an unofficial app for the Reachy Mini desktop robots, native on iPhone, iPad and Mac. It is not Pollen Robotics' own app, and it is not affiliated with, endorsed by or supported by Pollen Robotics or Hugging Face.

It talks to a robot on your own network directly, with no account to create. A Hugging Face sign-in is optional — for installing robot apps, and for reaching your robots from outside their network through its relay.

TRY IT WITHOUT A ROBOT

Under Developer on the Connect screen, "Start the simulator" opens a session with a robot the app carries itself — no robot, no network, no account. It is drawn from the robot's own description and moved by the same kinematics the app sends to real hardware. It has no camera, no app catalogue and no Wi-Fi setup, because those belong to a machine that does not exist.

A Reachy Mini Wireless on your network is what the whole app is for. A Lite model — or a daemon run in simulation on a computer — connects the same way, minus the routes only the wireless daemon serves.

WHAT IT DOES

• Connect — Nearby finds robots on your network with a sweep and Bonjour or at an address you type, and on a Mac the daemon on that computer. Remote reaches the robots linked to your Hugging Face account, wherever they are.

• Live control — joystick teleop of the 6-DoF head, the antennas and body rotation, with the robot's camera and two-way audio, so you can talk through its speaker. Let the head follow a face, at a strength you pick between a glance and a lock.

• 3D viewer — a RealityKit model built from the robot's own URDF and meshes, mirroring it in real time.

• Moves — browse and play the recorded moves the robot ships with, from the app or by asking Siri for one by name. Record your own takes with the joystick and play them back.

• Sounds — a soundboard for the robot's speaker: add audio files from your device and play them with a tap.

• Apps — install, update and remove robot apps from Hugging Face Spaces, following each job as it runs. Filter and sort the catalogue and pin the apps you use most.

• State and logs — the control loop's frequency, worst interval and error count charted live, beside the robot's own processor, memory, temperature and uptime. The daemon's own log streams in as it is written.

• Files — an SFTP browser for the robot's filesystem.

• Bluetooth setup and recovery — put a brand-new robot onto Wi-Fi over an encrypted Bluetooth channel, or bring back one that fell off the network.

AT HOME ON YOUR DEVICES

Widgets for the Home Screen, the Lock Screen, StandBy and the Mac's Notification Centre. The Mac also keeps the robot in the menu bar: awake or asleep, one button to change it, and the installed apps underneath. Control Center controls for power, for a move or an app you choose yourself, for a sound, and for stopping whatever is running — each one on the Lock Screen and the Action button too. Siri and Shortcuts for waking, sleeping, powering off, launching an app, playing a move, or asking whether the robot is awake and what is running on it, each able to name which robot it means. Sixteen animated Reachy stickers for Messages, the Stickers app and FaceTime. Six accent themes, each with a matching app icon and a colour for the 3D robot. English, German, Spanish, French and Russian.

PRIVACY

Nothing is collected. The app talks to your robot and, if you sign in, to Hugging Face with your own account. There is no server on our side.

A NOTE ON YOUR NETWORK

The robot's daemon provides no authentication and no encryption of its own. Use Hey Reachy on a trusted private network or on the robot's own access point — never through a port forward or a public address.

Hey Reachy is an independent client for the robot daemon's documented HTTP and WebSocket API. "Reachy Mini" is a product name of Pollen Robotics, used here solely to describe what this app is compatible with.

Requires iOS 18 or macOS 15.
whatsNew:
YOUR THEME ON THE ROBOT

Pick a theme in Settings → Appearance and the 3D robot takes its colour — body and head, in the live view and in the simulator alike. Graphite keeps the factory white, and the new Paint the 3D robot switch keeps it white under any theme. The robot on your desk stays as it is.

STICKERS

Sixteen Reachy characters land in Messages with the app — an astronaut, a cowboy, a jazzman and thirteen more, each with an animation of its own. They reach the Stickers app, the Messages camera and FaceTime as well, so they are not only for a conversation.

ON YOUR WRIST AND IN THE CAR

The running-app Live Activity now shows in the Apple Watch Smart Stack and on the CarPlay dashboard, with no Watch app to install.

FIXES

• Robots on software 1.11 no longer get a compatibility warning. When a robot is newer than the app was tested with, the warning is translated, names the tested version and sits right under Status.
• The motion sensor reading is more reliable: a robot restart no longer clears it, and a robot without one shows none instead of an error.
• Tapping a notification that an app finished installing or updating opens that app's page; a system update opens Settings.
• A Home Screen quick action tapped while the app was closed now runs once the robot connects, instead of being dropped.
promotionalText: Native on iPhone, iPad and Mac: joystick, camera and a live 3D twin for a Reachy Mini on your own network, no account needed — or the simulator inside the app.
